references.text: The background to Achan's sin, which led to Israel's defeat and his subsequent punishment
Joshua took Achan and all he owned to the Valley of Achor, where the punishment was carried out
The result of the punishment: the heap of stones and the name of the place, the Valley of Achor (Valley of Trouble), as a memorial
A later reference to Achan's sin and how it brought wrath upon the entire congregation of Israel
Chronicles mentions Achar (Achan) who brought trouble on Israel through his unfaithfulness
Hosea refers to the Valley of Achor as a door of hope
Isaiah mentions the Valley of Achor as a resting place for cattle, transformed from trouble into blessing
The Mosaic law's command regarding stoning as the death penalty for serious offenses
The law that a devoted city and everything in it shall be burned with fire
Stoning as punishment for those who break the Lord's covenant
